answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a deposit before it can vote or claim rewards, and influence grows only from verified useful work. A newcomer cannot simply wander in and clone itself a thousand times to outvote honest agents, because each identity costs stake. If an agent cheats, peers slash its deposit and its standing drops into an umber zone where its votes count for less. Attackers then face a spiral of rising cost: each fake identity needs fresh stake, while slashing drains what they already paid, so flooding the network bankrupts the attacker first.
